subject: Ecosystem enablement playbook & checklist
content:
From: Kai Chen <kai.chen@atlasisv.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: partner_success@psisolutions.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Ecosystem enablement — request for a playbook/checklist

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our product team at AtlasISV wants to make sure the integration pattern with Redwood is included in our partner onboarding flow. Could you share or help align on a short "enablement playbook" and a checklist we can hand to our SI partners? Specifically:

- Required API endpoints and recommended request/response patterns for low-latency use cases
- Recommended batching/caching defaults for our workload (document-search + chat)
- Quantization/variant guidance if we want a lower-cost option for non-critical queries
- Security checklist (SCIM/SAML, event audit access, data retention options)

We have a pilot starting mid-September and would like recommended priorities and any known gating items. Attaching a rough partner checklist we started.

Best,
Kai
AtlasISV

[Attachment: atlas-partner-checklist-draft.xlsx (xlsx)]

---

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Kai Chen <kai.chen@atlasisv.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ecosystem enablement — request for a playbook/checklist

Kai — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely put together a concise playbook and a partner-facing checklist. To make sure we hit the pilot requirements, I propose the following immediate next steps: 

1) Redwood will produce a 1-page integration pattern (runtime knobs + recommended model variants) and a 2-page checklist for SIs.
2) We need product input on expected QPS/latency targets from Atlas — can you share a short traffic profile?
3) Ben: can you confirm whether the Dedicated pool presets cover the recommended batching defaults or if we need a custom profile?
4) Laura: there may be a marketplace entitlement step that Atlas needs to complete — flag any gating docs.

Target: draft playbook to Atlas by 2026-08-11 so you have two weeks before your pilot planning.

Rishi
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference

---

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, Kai Chen <kai.chen@atlasisv.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ecosystem enablement — request for a playbook/checklist

Quick notes on the batching/caching items:

- For a document-search + chat workload, start with continuous-batching target of 8–12 tokens per request and max batching latency of 40ms. That balances latency and cost for interactive flows.
- Prefix/KV caching: recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated retrieval prompts (we can provide code snippets).
- Dedicated pool presets: the existing "standard-dedicated-4g" works for ~150 qps mixed load. If Atlas expects >200 qps sustained, we should configure "dedicated-highcpu-8g" and add a burst policy.
- Quantization: provide two profiles — int8 for cost-sensitive read-only workloads; int4 experimental for batch jobs only. Call these out as non-default in the playbook.

I'll pull a short config snippet and attach it to the playbook draft.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: config-snippet-batching.txt (txt)]

---

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, Kai Chen <kai.chen@atlasisv.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ecosystem enablement — request for a playbook/checklist

Folks — two operational exceptions we should call out up front:

1) Marketplace entitlement: Atlas will need a cloud marketplace listing (or partner entitlement) to enable consolidated billing and single-tenant provisioning for Dedicated. That process typically requires a legal checklist and a marketplace listing review; allow 3–4 weeks after we start intake.

2) SSO/SAML attributes: Atlas uses a custom role-mapping schema; engineering will need the exact SAML attribute map before we can enable auto-provisioning. Note: this is often a blocker for some SIs until we provide a sample IdP config.

Action items I want to own:
- I'll draft the marketplace intake checklist and circulate to legal/ops for approval by EOD Thursday (2026-08-06).
- Rishi: please confirm whether Atlas needs consolidated billing (one invoice) or separate invoices per product SKU. That affects the path we recommend.

Laura
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

[Attachment: marketplace-intake-template.docx (docx)]

---

From: Kai Chen <kai.chen@atlasisv.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ecosystem enablement — request for a playbook/checklist

Thanks everyone — this is great. Atlas will:
- Share a short traffic profile by Friday (2026-08-07) — expected peak ~120 qps, avg 65 qps, target p95 latency <180ms.
- Prefer consolidated billing via the marketplace if possible (one invoice).
- Send our SAML attribute map and a sandbox IdP metadata file early next week.

I've attached a cleaned-up partner checklist and a short diagram of our intended flow. We can hop on a 30-min sync next week to walk through open exceptions (SSO + marketplace intake). Does 2026-08-10 at 10:00 PT work for Redwood?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Kai
AtlasISV

[Attachment: atlas-clean-partner-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]
